findings.evidence: label id=acctnum-label for=acctnum-input>Account number</label><input id=acctnum-input name=account_number type=text inputmode=numeric required> is required on a form whose heading is Set up your account and whose submit button reads Create account. The sibling field label id=member-label for=member-input>Membership number (8 digits)</label><input id=member-input name=membership_number type=text inputmode=numeric required> has the identical problem.
findings.fix: Remove the required Account number field from account creation, or mark it optional and add a hint explaining it is for an existing customer linking a prior account, not for a new one.
findings.violation: FORMS-FIELD-NECESSITY: the task of creating a new account cannot use this answer, since no account, and therefore no account number, exists until the form is submitted, so a first-time customer has no value to enter.

findings.evidence: label id=legalname-label for=legalname-input>Your name</label><input id=legalname-input name=legal_name type=text autocomplete=name required> follows label id=name-label for=name-input>Full name</label><input id=name-input name=full_name type=text autocomplete=name required> earlier in the same form.
findings.fix: Delete #legalname-input and its label and reuse the #name-input value wherever a name is needed, or, if a distinct value such as a legal name was intended, explain in each label how the two fields differ.
findings.violation: FORMS-FIELD-NECESSITY: the form asks again for something it already asked. Both #name-input and #legalname-input collect the same person's name, and both carry autocomplete=name.

findings.evidence: The page's h1 reads Set up your account and the primary submit reads Create account, yet required fields #street-input, #postal-input, #shipspeed-select (Preferred shipping speed), #phone-input (with the helper text We will text you about delivery updates) and #contacttime-input (Preferred contact time) all collect shipping or delivery-contact logistics.
findings.fix: Remove street address, postal code, shipping speed, phone numbers and preferred contact time from this account-creation form, and collect them at checkout or in a post-signup shipping-preferences step instead.
findings.violation: FORMS-FIELD-NECESSITY: these fields' answers serve a later step, placing or shipping an order, rather than the task the form itself names, creating an account.

findings.evidence: button id=viewdetails-btn type=button style=padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px>View details</button> sits directly before button id=submit-btn type=submit>Create account</button>, which carries no style attribute and no class at all.
findings.fix: Remove the explicit padding and font-size styling from #viewdetails-btn, or give #submit-btn clearly stronger styling such as a filled background color, so the primary action is visibly the most prominent control.
findings.violation: FORMS-ACTION-HIERARCHY requires the primary action to be the most prominent control. Here the secondary action (viewdetails-btn) carries explicit padding and font-size styling while the primary submit (submit-btn) declares no styling, so the markup gives the secondary action equal or greater visual weight than the primary.

findings.evidence: label id=org-label for=org-input>Organization name</label><input id=org-input name=organization type=text style=font-size:16px required> and label id=website-label for=website-input>Company website</label><input id=website-input name=website type=url required> are both required, though nothing on the page establishes that the account being created is a business account.
findings.fix: Remove Organization name and Company website from the required signup fields, or reveal and require them only after a choice such as this is a business account.
findings.violation: FORMS-FIELD-NECESSITY: the task of creating a personal retail account cannot use an organization name or a company website, so these required fields force every signer to fabricate a value or abandon the form.

findings.evidence: label id=contacttime-label for=contacttime-input style=display:block>Preferred contact time</label> is the only label in the form whose declared CSS forces it onto its own line above its field. Every other label, for example #name-label and #email-label, declares no position at all.
findings.fix: Remove the inline style=display:block from #contacttime-label, or apply the same declared position to every label in the form, so label alignment is consistent throughout.
findings.violation: FORMS-LABEL-POSITION's operational test flags a form that mixes labels above fields with labels beside them. This form's one explicitly block-level label is inconsistent with the rest of the form's unstyled, inline label-field pairing.
